verdict.root_cause: mongodb-rate's pod was created fresh at ~15:01 by platform-automation and then terminated externally by SIGTERM (kill(2) from pid 0/uid 0) within seconds, twice: two clean WiredTiger startup cycles at 15:01:02 and 15:01:04 each ended in signal-handler-driven orderly shutdown, the last at 15:01:10 [tr_9948fd3a2026][tr_fcd9d6881852]. The service itself logged no errors and its storage engine opened, recovered and checkpointed cleanly, so neither corruption, disk, nor storage misconfiguration is the mechanism [tr_fcd9d6881852][tr_4d3c551d555b]. The change set is a first-time workload creation accompanied by a ConfigMap whose name indicates fault-injection/failure-administration intent, landing seconds before the container came up [tr_616998c15f26]. The best-supported reading is an injected/administered kill of the mongodb-rate process: the datastore is absent from the topology while its socket/endpoint churns, leaving callers in the hotel-reservation namespace without a rate datastore. With no metrics available for this service at all [tr_596c016954c3], the mechanism is the process being stopped/killed rather than any value being wrong.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent log cuts agree the process was healthy at the storage layer and died to an external signal with no self-reported error, which excludes OOM/segfault (handled SIGTERM path), disk_fill and datastore_corruption (clean recovery, checkpoint, no space or parse errors), and bad_deploy (engine config byte-identical across both starts, first creation rather than a rolling update). The change log places an automation-authored fault-injection-named ConfigMap seconds before the container started, which is evidence for a deliberately induced stop of the process rather than a wrong configuration value doing work in the request path. Remediation is to bring the process back and keep it running (remove the injected kill and restart the workload).
open_questions: Whether the SIGTERM came from the fault-injection ConfigMap, normal Kubernetes pod lifecycle/rescheduling during first creation, or a liveness-probe failure - no kubelet or pod-event evidence was gathered.
Whether mongodb-rate stayed down after 15:01:10 or recovered; the log window ends at 15:02:30 and no post-onset startup was observed.
Which callers (e.g. rate service) actually degraded, and whether they hung to deadline or failed fast - no upstream metrics or logs were dispatched.
What alert fired at 15:02:21 and on what signal, given Prometheus holds no series for this service [tr_596c016954c3].

alternatives.root_cause: The PVC rate-pvc was created and updated twice within seconds, and the resulting volume rebind forced the pod to be torn down and rescheduled repeatedly.
alternatives.why_not: Both engine opens succeeded against a mounted, readable data path with clean journal recovery, so no storage configuration value was actually wrong at the point of failure [tr_fcd9d6881852].

alternatives.root_cause: A lowered memory limit on the newly created workload caused the container runtime to terminate mongodb repeatedly.
alternatives.why_not: The teardown follows the handled SIGTERM path with a full ordered shutdown and only 3 in-flight operations interrupted; an OOM kill would be SIGKILL with no such sequence [tr_9948fd3a2026].

proposal.expected_effect: No action taken, so nothing changes. A restart would only be verifiable if a post-restart mongod startup in Loki were NOT followed within ~10s by a SignalHandler shutdown - but we never saw whether mongodb-rate recovered after 15:01:10 (log window ends 15:02:30), and no metrics exist for this service, so the effect is currently unobservable.
proposal.if_wrong: If a Loki query past 15:02:30 shows mongodb-rate still absent or looping startup/SIGTERM, and a kubelet/pod-event check shows no external killer still active, then restart_service becomes justified and this abstention was too cautious. Conversely, if pod events name the fault-injection ConfigMap as the killer, a restart would be re-killed and the fix lies outside this system.
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves the rate datastore down if it never came back, so hotel-reservation callers keep failing. Restarting instead would risk recreating a container that the still-active external killer terminates again, masking the real cause and burning the one-shot (irreversible) restart while confidence is low.
proposal.blast_radius: No one sees a change now. Any later restart touches mongodb-rate only, with callers in the hotel-reservation namespace (the rate service) seeing connection resets during recreate.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A single warning on a datastore's rate metric is not clearly a benign latency blip, and a database-level anomaly can precede broader failure, so it is not safe to dismiss. No open incident matches and nothing in the signal points to a specific fault class yet.
